about: What the Wadees say to you (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-16-wadoo-design.md §6). who: a name, @role, #trait (grief, shy) or * for anyone. when: facts of WadooState.facts() that must equal the value; min:<fact> at least it, max:<fact> at most it. The most specific line that holds is spoken (a name over a trait over a role over anyone, then more conditions); a speaker with several equally specific goes through them in turn. {name} is the speaker, {deeds} what you did for them. then: what speaking it does; a choice's answers say their own lines and do their own then. A line with no hostile condition is spoken only while they are not hostile.

pages: They will not look at you.
Your ship was loud. Loud things bring it out of the sand. Be glad it went deep.
We do not get many from the sky. The pool is for drinking, not for feet.
The sun is strong today. Every cell in Wadoo will be full by the time the shadows turn.
Looking for the queen? Her hall is the tall one at the head of the north court. Oru will not let you in.
Six of us, in one dark hour. Forgive me. I have work.
They say you helped. Wadoo remembers that.
Sit with us in the shade sometime. The benches are old, but they hold.
Even the Sunguard nodded at you today. I saw it.
You stood before Imsa. Not many from outside ever have.
You go with Kesh? Then the sun go with you.
Bring them all home. That is all I ask of you.
...Oh. Hello. You are very tall in that suit.
Halla says you are kind. I believe Halla.
We have no flowers left to lay for them. The sun-lilies at the edge of the north garden open one at a time, and we cannot wait for them.
There is a lily at the stones. Was it you? Thank you.
Keep your hands where I can see them, sky-walker.
This staff holds a whole day of sun. Do not make me spend it.
You have done right by us. I stand easier.
Kesh waits at the breach. We go when you say.
I am Kesh. I hold the breach until it is walled again. Do not stand in it.
You are the one who helps. Good. Help faster. The breach will not wall itself.
When you are ready, we go.
The queen does not receive strangers. Help our people, and they will speak for you.
They speak well of you. Go in.
The queen has seen you. The door stays open to you.
The others are at the breach. I keep her door until we are back.
The gate is the way in. The breach is the beast's way. Use mine.
I carried two of them back in through that breach. Do not ask me which two.
The pool is the heart of Wadoo. I watch it as you would watch your own heart.
The beast trod on the pump's sun cell, and my garden died of thirst.
Daro has a new cell cooling at the Glassworks. These old knees will not carry it, and his hands are full.
Daro's cell! Oh, look at it shine.
The pump is there, by my dry bed: the stone well with the bronze frame. Set the cell in the cage at the top.
Hear it? The pump! Look at the beans drink. You have a good back, sky-walker.
Sand, sun and patience: that is all glass is. Halla's pump needs a new cell, and this one is ready.
I have set it by the Glassworks door. Carry it to her pump, at the dry garden by the east wall. Mind the cage: the glass holds a whole day of sun.
The cell is by the Glassworks door. Halla's pump is at the dry garden, by the east wall.
Two hands. Good. The pump is at Halla's dry garden, by the east wall.
That cell will outlast me. Good work deserves good work.
My mother Ruma's armlet: bronze, with a water stone. I lost it when we ran.
It is out past the breach, where the tracks are. I cannot go out there. Not yet.
Her armlet. You went out there for it.
I will wear it every day. She would have liked you.
If you are hurt, come to me. Water and a little sun mend most things.
Sit. Let me see you.
There: water from the deep pool, and a little sun. You will mend.
My sister Inka made the lamps at the stones. Now they burn for her.
Mada and I were to plant the east beds together this season. I plant them alone.
My brother Orin ran toward it. He always ran toward things.
Bel was faster than any of us. It did not matter.
The water stone is for the oasis. We wear it so the water knows us.
Halla taught me to grow beans in sand. Halla taught everyone everything.
A good sunglass rings when you tap it. A bad one only clicks. Listen.
Every stone of that wall was carried here by someone's grandmother. We will carry them again.
Have you eaten? You look like someone who forgets to.
Daro says I have the hands for glass. Daro says that to everyone.
Wash at the pool's edge, never in it. That is the first thing a Wadee learns.
The Listening House heard it coming. Too late, but it heard it. Next time it will hear sooner.
Who let you in? Oru! Leave my hall.
So you are the one my people speak of. {deeds}. Wadoo has not had a guest in a long while. Be welcome.
Hear me, then. In the dark before the last moon, something came out of the dunes. The Listening House heard it too late: a sound like the sand breathing.
It crushed two homes and broke our wall. It took six of us before the Sunguard drove it off with the fire of the sun. Then it went under the sand.
It hears the ground, and it hears ships. When your ship came down, it went deep. A ship will never find it. Feet might.

choice.ask: Will you hunt it with my Sunguard, on foot?

reply: Then go to the breach. Kesh and the Sunguard will meet you there. Wadoo will not forget this.
Then I will wait. The beast will not.

pages: You have come back.

pages: Kesh is waiting at the breach. Go with the sun.
Leave my hall.
